title: [17/10/2025] English language learning trend across three countries
prompt: The charts show the difference in how three countries learn English in 2010 and 2015. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the percentages of three methods used for learning English—evening classes, online courses, and studying abroad—in three different countries in 2010 and 2015.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, evening classes consistently represented the dominant learning method in all three nations throughout the period, although their popularity declined universally. In contrast, online learning gained substantial traction across the board, while studying abroad exhibited varying trends. Notably, Country C showed the strongest preference for evening classes, while Country B experienced the most pronounced transformation in its learning patterns.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding evening classes, in 2010, this method accounted for 70% and 72% of learners in Countries A and B respectively, while Country C recorded a significantly higher figure of 94%. By 2015, all three countries witnessed decreases, with Country A dropping marginally to 67% and Country C falling to 82%, whereas Country B saw a dramatic decline to 48%. Turning to online learning, this approach represented only 5% in Country A, 8% in Country B, and 6% in Country C in 2010. However, over the five-year period, these proportions doubled in Country A to reach 10%, quadrupled in Country B to 32%, and increased more than twofold in Country C to 15%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for studying abroad, in 2010, Country A had the highest proportion at 25%, followed by Country B at 20%, while Country C recorded no learners using this method. By 2015, the proportion going overseas declined slightly in A, remained unchanged in B at one fifth, and rose only modestly in C to 3%, meaning this route was always the least favoured in all three nations.
